newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Kingstream says gets state agreement.
newsitem.headline: Kingstream says gets state agreement.

text.p: Kingstream Resources NL said on Wednesday that it had signed an agreement with the Western Australia state government providing assurances for its proposed Midwest Iron and Steel project.

The agreement provides a framework for the A$1.4 billion project to ensure long-term security of tenure for mining tenements, access to sevices and infrastructure and a secure means of supply of gas, electricity and water, Kingstream said.
The agreement requires Kingstream and its merged entity, An Feng Steel Co Ltd of Taiwan, to submit a detailed proposal to the state by December 31, 1998, it said.
"The financial arrangements should be in place by the end of the second quarter, the 30th of June," Kingstream chairman Ken Court told Reuters.
Court said the steelmaking project, to be located in Geraldton, north of Perth, would be financed using a combination of 70 percent debt and 30 percent equity.
The debt funding would be supplied by a consortium of banks.
Court said he was confident of obtaining financing for the project, targeted to produce 2.4 million tonnes of steel slab a year.
"The feasibility study shows the project is in the lowest quartile of cost production of field plants around the world," Court said.
